title_or_table: Ranked-choice voting (RCV), section 'State laws prohibiting RCV'
observation_period: State law as of November 2026, the as-of date Ballotpedia states. The same 19 states appear in Atlas V7 repair log row RL47 as of October 15, 2026
geography: 50 states and the District of Columbia (one row each)
universe_or_base: Statewide laws or constitutional provisions that prohibit ranked-choice voting
unit: prohibits_rcv is 1 or 0; scope is all or some
qualification: 17 of the 19 bans cover all elections. Ohio's leaves an opening for home-rule cities, at the cost of state funds, and Tennessee's names statewide and local offices only

prohibits_rcv.description: 1 when the state bans ranked-choice voting, else 0

scope.description: all (every election) or some (some elections); empty when there is no ban

enacted_date.description: date the ban took effect or was signed, as Ballotpedia prints it

measure.description: bill or measure, as Ballotpedia prints it

printed_source_line: Source: Ballotpedia, Ranked-choice voting (RCV), state laws prohibiting RCV, as of November 2026, 50 states and DC. Retrieved November 6, 2026. Ohio’s and Tennessee’s bans cover some elections; the other 17 cover all.
scope_rule: all means the law, as Ballotpedia quotes it, covers local, state and federal offices or every election in the state. some means the quoted text leaves a class of elections out. Exceptions for military and overseas voters' ranked runoff ballots (Alabama, Arkansas, Louisiana) do not change the scope
first_choice_source: Atlas V7 source W049, the National Conference of State Legislatures page https://www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/ranked-choice-voting, returned HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare security challenge on November 6, 2026. The studio did not retry it. NCSL's own state list and scope labels were not read
v7_comparison: Same 19 states and the same enactment years as V7 RL47. V7 gives the count of 19 from NCSL (March 23, 2026)

primary_checks.Tennessee: Read on the Tennessee General Assembly site: SB1820, Public Chapter 621, 'prohibits a county election commission from utilizing instant runoff voting or ranked choice voting to conduct an election in this state for a statewide or local government office'; signed by the governor 02/28/2022; Pub. Ch. 621 on 03/07/2022
primary_checks.Mississippi: billstatus.ls.state.ms.us failed TLS certificate verification; not read
primary_checks.Ohio: www.legislature.ohio.gov failed TLS certificate verification; not read
primary_checks.Missouri: A guessed Secretary of State URL for Amendment 7 returned 404; the amendment text was not read

unconfirmed: Every state except Tennessee rests on Ballotpedia's quotation of the statute; the statutes themselves were not read
Alabama's bill number prints as 'SB 1886' on Ballotpedia; not checked against the Alabama Legislature
Ballotpedia gives two bill numbers for Iowa (HF 954 and HF 1954) and two signing dates for North Dakota (April 15 and April 18, 2025)
Missouri's scope rests on Ballotpedia's statement that Amendment 7 'prohibited ranked-choice voting'
Mississippi's quoted text does not name congressional district races; marked all as Ballotpedia describes it
